newsitem.title: USA: U.S. must pry open Chinese market-Commerce's Daley.
newsitem.headline: U.S. must pry open Chinese market-Commerce's Daley.

text.p: Commerce Secretary William Daley said Wednesday that U.S. exports to China rose a modest two percent last year and that Washington must continue to press China to open its markets to more U.S. goods.

"China's market remains far too closed to our exports," Daley said in a statement after the government released trade figures for 1996. "We must make every effort in every forum to continue to pry open the Chinese market."
For all of 1996, the overall U.S. trade deficit rose 8.7 percent to $114.23 billion, the highest since 1988's $115.5 billion, the government said.

Daley said the rise in the trade deficit for 1996 was due to higher oil prices. He also said strong sustained U.S. economic growth and the faltering growth of most of U.S. trading partners also contributed to the trade deficit.
